understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete each KA59 level by maneuvering the selectable pieces so that every goal tile marked with a '+' in the semantic grid was occupied by a selectable piece at the same time, progressing through all levels until the engine reported WIN for the full run.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each action moved the currently selected piece one grid cell (3 pixels) in the chosen direction, with x increasing to the right and y increasing downward. Walls ('#') acted as impassable obstacles that could block movement; blocks ('B') could be pushable if adjacent in the movement direction, shifting along with the piece when pushed, otherwise causing a block. Levels could contain multiple selectable pieces (P for the selected one, S for other selectables), and control could be switched by using CLICK on the exact pixel-coordinate position of another selectable. The movement.*_blocked flags were only hints about adjacency and did not guarantee success/failure, so testing moves was sometimes necessary to learn how boundaries and objects behaved.

understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete each KA59 level by maneuvering the selectable pieces so that every goal tile marked with a '+' in the semantic grid was occupied by a selectable piece at the same time, progressing through all levels until the engine reported WIN for the full run.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each action moved the currently selected piece one grid cell (3 pixels) in the chosen direction, with x increasing to the right and y increasing downward. Walls ('#') acted as impassable obstacles that could block movement; blocks ('B') could be pushable if adjacent in the movement direction, shifting along with the piece when pushed, otherwise causing a block. Levels could contain multiple selectable pieces (P for the selected one, S for other selectables), and control could be switched by using CLICK on the exact pixel-coordinate position of another selectable. The movement.*_blocked flags were only hints about adjacency and did not guarantee success/failure, so testing moves was sometimes necessary to learn how boundaries and objects behaved.
